explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/497 (Dedekind's problem): how many antichains of subsets of [n] are there? Kleitman proved 2^{(1+o(1))C(n,⌊n/2⌋)}. DedekindNumber.M' n counts Sperner families in Finset (Fin n); the tests give 2, 3, 6, 20, the Dedekind numbers. The statement asserts an o(1) function o with M' n = 2^{(1+o n)·C(n, n/2)} for all n. That is well-posed because M' n ≥ 2 and the binomial is ≥ 1, so o can be defined pointwise. Faithful.
